summary: Partial ack loss during chained tool invocations results in silent retries and duplicate external webhook side-effects
description: Issue summary: Customer runs a multi-step orchestration where the model is asked to call two external tools in sequence (1) a synchronous DB write via a webhook and (2) a long-running external job kickoff via a webhook. During streaming responses the SDK client experiences a partial-ack (ACK) for the first tool call but the final stream disconnects before the server confirms the overall request completion. Impact: The customer's webhook for step (1) receives the POST and performs a side-effect (payment capture). After the streaming reconnect, SDKs retry the request and the webhook receives a second POST, causing duplicate side-effects. This happens inconsistently and appears correlated with client reconnects from mobile networks. Environment: Production using Python SDK v1.9.3 and Go SDK v0.8.4 behind an API Gateway. Customer is on an enterprise plan with reserved Dedicated capacity in us-east.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure orchestration that issues two tool calls sequentially from a single streamed generation: first webhook A (synchronous side-effect), then webhook B (async job kickoff).
2) Use Python SDK with streaming=true and set small TCP keepalive timeouts to emulate flaky mobile network.
3) Trigger generation and forcibly interrupt the stream mid-output (simulate network blip).
4) Reconnect client and let SDK perform its default retry behavior without providing explicit idempotency keys.
5) Observe webhook A receiving duplicate POSTs and performing duplicate side-effects; webhook B sometimes receives duplicate job kickoffs as well.
logs: 2025-02-14T18:02:11Z API-GW INFO request_id=abc123 stream_disconnected before final ACK; upstream returned 200 for tool_call webhook_A
2025-02-14T18:02:11Z serving-runtime DEBUG request_id=abc123 tool_call[0] -> external POST 200 {trace_id: tx-987}
2025-02-14T18:02:13Z sdk-python WARN reconnect attempt=1 request_id=abc123 retrying full request (no idempotency key provided)
2025-02-14T18:02:13Z external-webhook INFO webhook_A processed payment capture order_id=H-55-02 (duplicate after retry)
2025-02-14T18:02:14Z sdk-go INFO reconnect success request_id=abc123 new_request_id=abc123-r2
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SDK retry logic resends entire user request when stream is interrupted and server does not return a final success marker; tool calls inside the generation are therefore re-executed unless idempotency metadata is included.

Observed that serving-runtime acknowledges individual tool_call dispatch to external webhook with internal logs, but the client sees only stream-level success/failure. If stream-level handshake is lost, client retries the outer request causing duplicate downstream side-effects.
Reproduced locally with Python SDK v1.9.3 by simulating TCP RST; confirmed duplicate POST to webhook when no idempotency key provided.
Go SDK behaves similarly when configured to auto-retry; differences observed in default retry backoff timing causing varied duplication rates.
No evidence of server replay from queue/backoff — duplicates originate from client-side retry of the full generation call.
comments: Customer (Nimbus Health) 2025-02-14: 'We observed two payment captures for the same order after a mobile client lost connection. We need guidance to avoid financial duplicates.'
Support (Maya) 2025-02-14: 'Thanks — we're investigating. Can you share SDK versions and sample request payloads? Also provide timestamps of duplicate webhook calls.'

SRE (Diego) 2025-02-15: 'Attached traces show tool_call dispatch completed server-side before stream tear — client retried. Recommending idempotency keys for external webhook calls and short-term mitigation by disabling automatic full-request retries in SDK.'
Eng (Elena Novak) 2025-02-16: 'We should add guidance and an SDK helper to surface per-tool-call idempotency metadata and a pattern for at-most-once side-effects on streamed requests.'
Customer 2025-02-17: 'Implementing a per-tool idempotency token helped; still seeing rare duplicates when reconnection logic triggers immediate retransmit. Need server-side protection too.'
resolution: Workaround: Advise customer to include per-tool idempotency tokens in tool_call metadata (x-idempotency-token) and to disable client automatic full-request retries until SDK update. Implemented temporary webhook-side dedupe window (idempotency cache keyed by token) on customer's endpoint.
